sourceOccurrences.relationship: Source-inspected exposition with explicit scope distinctions
sourceOccurrences.note: 7902 allows arbitrary deleted sets and endpoints; 67GX requires normalized off-diagonal rows and uniformly finite susceptibility for its real quotient. Empty sets and zero intensity use totalized real division. Later random-cluster and derivative arguments are separate.

sourceOccurrences.label: Finite-volume susceptibility derivative
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Source-inspected exposition with explicit scope distinctions
sourceOccurrences.note: TAVM is obtained from finite-coordinate Russo and two oriented pivotal witnesses. The ambient vertex type is arbitrary. A right derivative is included at zero; the two-sided derivative is asserted only at positive intensity. Infinite-volume identities and stronger lower derivative bounds are separate.

proofUses.reason: Use last exits, fresh added coordinates and the correct outside continuation endpoints; sum before passing to countable volume.

Sublattice domination proves a finite threshold. The density bound 67W9 and written right continuity give a positive critical density; positive isolation probability makes the lower threshold bound strict.
An embedded plane, the heavy-edge theorem, closed cuts and the inverse-square theorem give the classification. Sharpness identifies the susceptibility endpoint; finite-cluster atoms give continuity.
Local chain rules and endpoint divergence integrate the corrected square; the logarithmic antiderivative first gives a polynomial bound, avoiding a circular logarithm substitution.
The finite-volume pivotal derivative formula (6JBS) is bounded uniformly by finite-coordinate BK (BNY8), passed to the limit by dominated convergence, and translated to the root.
Conditioning on K_x gives the expectation identity; the deletion bound (7902) and the three-point tree-graph inequality (L82Q) give the five-factor error.
The five-factor bound J1LW is weighted by J(o,y) and summed, with the two-cluster identity (4800) identifying the main term with chi'.
Integration of the differential inequality for 1/chi using monotonicity of chi; no other wiki assertion is invoked.
The reciprocal integral in the integrated bound TC6Q is restricted to a short interval where the diagram bound controls D.
Sprinkling an independent sparse layer and MLLO give right-openness; the row-sum bound (E771) gives b_chi>=1/L, and monotone coupling gives endpoint divergence.
A Peierls dual-cycle count with a union bound and a path count for the lower bound; no other wiki assertion is invoked.
The Peierls bound on a retained coordinate plane (NUJY) gives beta_c finite; 5LNL gives the row-sum lower bound and endpoint divergence.
A growing-block renormalisation with a union-bound recursion gives an infinite cluster; the row-sum bound (JZ47) gives beta_c>0.

Above p_c every finite-set functional is at least one by the threshold identification L0TE; the wired-boundary calculation (HATE) with the homogeneous Russo formula (4IHK) gives the differential inequality that is integrated.
Below p_c(G) the finite-set characterisation (RDF0) gives a contracting set, transported by the local isomorphism, and the certificate bound (YLZV) gives finite susceptibility on G_n.
Direct integration and a comparison of the lattice sum with the integral; no other wiki assertion is invoked.

Multiscale good-block renormalization: overlapping good blocks merge, two disjoint bad blocks are a squared error, and a single bad spot is bridged by one long edge whose failure probability is bounded through the inverse-square block integral (PAFY).

A renormalization inequality for crossings by short edges, with bridges bounded through the inverse-square tail and Harris for decreasing events, keeps the non-crossing probability bounded below; closed long edges and the zero-one law then exclude percolation when the tail coefficient times the squared density is below one.
